pr.title: feat(cake_mla_value_gate): add an experimental fused MLA value projection + sigmoid gate
pr.body:
This adds `cake_mla_value_gate`, an experimental FlashInfer primitive for MLA decode. In one kernel it computes the value projection of the merged BF16 latent `[B, H, 512]` with `W_UV` `[H, 512, 128]` (FP32 accumulation, explicit BF16 rounding), an FP32 sigmoid of the BF16 gate logits, the multiply, and zeroing of rows with `valid_lengths <= 0`. It writes a caller-owned BF16 `[B, H*128]` output that matches SGLang's fused `MlaValue` consumer bit for bit. The first baseline is the strongest FlashInfer composition: `bmm_bf16` on the strided latent view (fastest per row among the auto, cudnn and tgv backends, autotuned or not), then a `torch.compile`d FP32 sigmoid gate with valid-row zeroing. The second is SGLang's fused `MlaValue` kernel (sgl-project/sglang#48510), the consumer this primitive is proposed for in #8795. On GB300 the new kernel is faster than the FlashInfer composition on all 96 rows, at 1.29x-3.10x with per-mode medians of 1.82x (warm standalone), 2.28x (warm, behind PDL), 1.81x (cold standalone) and 2.70x (cold, behind PDL). It is also faster than `MlaValue` on all 96 rows, at 1.06x-1.53x with medians of 1.15x, 1.20x, 1.10x and 1.51x. On B200 it is faster than the FlashInfer composition on all 96 rows, at 1.27x-3.02x with medians of 1.82x, 2.23x, 1.80x and 2.61x. Against `MlaValue` on B200 it ranges from 1.05x to 1.59x with medians of 1.14x, 1.19x, 1.09x and 1.49x. It is faster on 95 rows and within measurement noise on one (cold L2 standalone, contiguous, B = 1: 1.05x). On B300, the target GPU of sgl-project/sglang#48510, it is faster than the FlashInfer composition on all 96 rows, at 1.28x-2.85x with medians of 1.85x, 2.30x, 1.82x and 2.72x, and faster than `MlaValue` on all 96 rows, at 1.06x-1.53x with medians of 1.15x, 1.20x, 1.10x and 1.50x.

+
+"""Benchmark the experimental MLA value projection + sigmoid output gate (SM100 / SM103).
+
+For every decode width ``B`` (``H = 12`` heads, one Kimi-K3 TP8 rank, unless
+``--heads``) this reports the complete call ``runner.launch(latent, gate,
+valid_lengths, out)`` replayed from a CUDA graph: CUPTI kernel time, median
+over the measured iterations, with the L2 flushed before every iteration
+unless ``--warm-l2``.  The flush needs CUPTI (``cupti-python`` >= 13); without
+it the script refuses a cold-L2 run, and a ``--warm-l2`` run falls back to
+CUDA-event timing of the graph replays.  The gate is the last ``H * 128``
+columns of a ``[B, pitch]`` fused projection output (``--gate-pitch 3648``,
+the default: ``projected[:, 2112:]`` at ``H = 12``) or a dense
+``[B, H * 128]`` tensor (``--gate-pitch`` equal to ``H * 128``).  Every row is
+valid.  The bandwidth column counts the bytes the call must move (``w_uv``,
+``latent``, the gate and ``out``).  ``--baseline unfused`` adds the unfused
+composition on the same tensors under the same protocol: ``torch.bmm`` into
+the ``[B, H * 128]`` output layout, then the FP32 sigmoid gate, the BF16
+rounding and the padded-row zeroing as elementwise torch operations.
+
+Usage::
+
+    python benchmarks/bench_cake_mla_value_gate.py [--rows 1 2 ...] [--heads 12]
+        [--gate-pitch 3648] [--no-pdl] [--warm-l2] [--baseline none|unfused]
+        [--json out.json]
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import statistics
+
+import torch
+
+from flashinfer.cake_mla_value_gate import prepare_mla_value_gate
+from flashinfer.testing import bench_gpu_time_with_cupti
+
+
+def _cupti_available() -> bool:
+    """True when CUPTI >= 13 is importable: the per-iteration L2 flush needs it."""
+    try:
+        from importlib.metadata import version
+
+        from cupti import cupti  # noqa: F401
+
+        return int(version("cupti-python").split(".")[0]) >= 13
+    except (ImportError, ValueError):
+        return False
+
+
+# The owner's decode widths.
+ROWS = (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 16, 32, 48, 64)
+LATENT, VALUE = 512, 128
+
+
+def _inputs(rows, heads, pitch, seed=42):
+    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
+    width = heads * VALUE
+    w_uv = (
+        (torch.randn((heads, VALUE, LATENT), generator=g) * 0.05)
+        .to(torch.bfloat16)
+        .cuda()
+        .transpose(1, 2)
+    )
+    latent = torch.randn((rows, heads, LATENT), generator=g).to(torch.bfloat16).cuda()
+    projected = (
+        (torch.randn((rows, pitch), generator=g) * 4.0).to(torch.bfloat16).cuda()
+    )
+    gate = projected[:, pitch - width :]
+    valid_lengths = torch.ones(rows, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    out = torch.empty((rows, width), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+    return w_uv, latent, gate, valid_lengths, out
+
+
+def _timed(fn, cold_l2):
+    times = bench_gpu_time_with_cupti(fn, use_cuda_graph=True, cold_l2_cache=cold_l2)
+    return float(statistics.median(times))
+
+
+def _unfused(w_uv, latent, gate, valid_lengths, out):
+    rows, heads, _ = latent.shape
+    projection = torch.empty_like(out)
+
+    def run():
+        # [H, B, 512] x [H, 512, 128] -> the [B, H * 128] layout, BF16-rounded once.
+        torch.bmm(
+            latent.transpose(0, 1),
+            w_uv,
+            out=projection.view(rows, heads, VALUE).transpose(0, 1),
+        )
+        gated = projection.float() * torch.sigmoid(gate.float())
+        gated.masked_fill_((valid_lengths <= 0)[:, None], 0.0)
+        out.copy_(gated)
+
+    return run
+
+
+def bench_row(rows, heads, pitch, enable_pdl, cold_l2, baseline):
+    w_uv, latent, gate, valid_lengths, out = _inputs(rows, heads, pitch)
+    runner = prepare_mla_value_gate(
+        w_uv, max_rows=64, sigmoid_precision="fp32", enable_pdl=enable_pdl
+    )
+    runner.launch(latent, gate, valid_lengths, out)  # load the program
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    width = heads * VALUE
+    nbytes = 2 * (heads * LATENT * VALUE + rows * heads * LATENT + 2 * rows * width)
+    call_ms = _timed(lambda: runner.launch(latent, gate, valid_lengths, out), cold_l2)
+    record = {
+        "rows": rows,
+        "heads": heads,
+        "gate_pitch": pitch,
+        "arch": runner.arch,
+        "program": runner.program,
+        "enable_pdl": enable_pdl,
+        "l2": "cold" if cold_l2 else "warm",
+        "call_us_median": call_ms * 1e3,
+        "call_gbps": nbytes / (call_ms * 1e-3) / 1e9,
+    }
+    if baseline == "unfused":
+        record["unfused_us_median"] = (
+            _timed(_unfused(w_uv, latent, gate, valid_lengths, out), cold_l2) * 1e3
+        )
+        record["speedup_vs_unfused"] = (
+            record["unfused_us_median"] / record["call_us_median"]
+        )
+    return record
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
+        description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--rows", type=int, nargs="+", default=list(ROWS))
+    parser.add_argument("--heads", type=int, default=12)
+    parser.add_argument("--gate-pitch", type=int, default=3648)
+    parser.add_argument("--no-pdl", action="store_true")
+    parser.add_argument("--warm-l2", action="store_true")
+    parser.add_argument("--baseline", default="none", choices=("none", "unfused"))
+    parser.add_argument("--json", type=str, default=None)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    if args.gate_pitch < args.heads * VALUE or args.gate_pitch % 2:
+        parser.error(f"--gate-pitch must be even and at least {args.heads * VALUE}")
+    cupti = _cupti_available()
+    if not args.warm_l2 and not cupti:
+        parser.error(
+            "a cold-L2 run flushes the L2 through CUPTI: install cupti-python >= 13 "
+            "or pass --warm-l2"
+        )
+    timer = "CUPTI" if cupti else "CUDA events"
+    records = [
+        bench_row(
+            rows,
+            args.heads,
+            args.gate_pitch,
+            not args.no_pdl,
+            not args.warm_l2,
+            args.baseline,
+        )
+        for rows in args.rows
+    ]
+    first = records[0]
+    print(
+        f"{torch.cuda.get_device_name()}  {first['arch']}  CUDA {torch.version.cuda}  "
+        f"H={args.heads}  gate pitch {args.gate_pitch}  L2 {first['l2']}  "
+        f"PDL {'on' if first['enable_pdl'] else 'off'}  timer {timer}"
+    )
+    header = f"{'B':>4}{'call us':>10}{'GB/s':>8}"
+    if args.baseline == "unfused":
+        header += f"{'unfused us':>12}{'speedup':>9}"
+    print(header)
+    for r in records:
+        line = f"{r['rows']:>4}{r['call_us_median']:>10.2f}{r['call_gbps']:>8.0f}"
+        if args.baseline == "unfused":
+            line += f"{r['unfused_us_median']:>12.2f}{r['speedup_vs_unfused']:>9.2f}"
+        print(line)
+    if args.json:
+        with open(args.json, "w") as handle:
+            json.dump(
+                {
+                    "device": torch.cuda.get_device_name(),
+                    "cuda": torch.version.cuda,
+                    "timer": timer,
+                    "rows": records,
+                },
+                handle,
+                indent=1,
+            )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+
+
+def main():
+    torch.manual_seed(42)
+    heads, rows, max_rows = 12, 8, 64  # one Kimi-K3 TP8 rank, eight decode tokens
+    # The absorbed value weight: the [H, 512, 128] view of a contiguous [H, 128, 512] tensor.
+    w_uv = (
+        (torch.randn(heads, 128, 512, device="cuda") * 0.05)
+        .to(torch.bfloat16)
+        .transpose(1, 2)
+    )
+    # Persistent buffers of the largest decode width; a call uses their first rows.
+    latent_buf = torch.randn(max_rows, heads, 512, device="cuda").to(torch.bfloat16)
+    # The gate logits are the last 1536 columns of the fused [B, 3648] projection output.
+    projected = torch.randn(max_rows, 3648, device="cuda").to(torch.bfloat16)
+    out_buf = torch.empty(max_rows, heads * 128, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+    # One length per request; a length <= 0 marks a padded request, whose row is
+    # written as zero.
+    valid_lengths = torch.tensor(
+        [17, 5, 0, 9, 33, -1, 1, 2], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"
+    )
+
+    # Prepare once, outside CUDA graph capture: binds w_uv and loads the program.
+    runner = prepare_mla_value_gate(w_uv, max_rows=max_rows, sigmoid_precision="fp32")
+    latent, gate, out = latent_buf[:rows], projected[:rows, 2112:], out_buf[:rows]
+
+    # The launch allocates nothing and runs on the current stream: capture it and replay it
+    # with new contents in the same buffers.
+    runner.launch(latent, gate, valid_lengths, out)
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+        runner.launch(latent, gate, valid_lengths, out)
+    latent.copy_(torch.randn_like(latent, dtype=torch.float32).to(torch.bfloat16))
+    graph.replay()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+
+    # Unfused reference: the BF16 projection times the FP32 sigmoid, padded rows zero.
+    value = torch.einsum("bhk,hkv->bhv", latent.float(), w_uv.float())
+    value = value.to(torch.bfloat16).float().reshape(rows, heads * 128)
+    reference = (value * torch.sigmoid(gate.float())).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    reference[valid_lengths <= 0] = 0
+    torch.testing.assert_close(out, reference, atol=1e-2, rtol=1e-2)
+    print(
+        "MLA value gate:",
+        tuple(out.shape),
+        out.dtype,
+        runner.arch,
+        runner.program,
+    )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":

+# Cake MLA value projection + sigmoid output gate (experimental, SM100 / SM103)
+
+Generated-program backend for the decode tail of gated multi-head latent
+attention (Kimi-K3): the per-head value up-projection of the attention's
+latent output fused with the sigmoid output gate, in one launch.
+
+Both the API and the backend are experimental (see
+[`../README.md`](../README.md)).  Calling
+`flashinfer.cake_mla_value_gate.prepare_mla_value_gate` is the opt-in; no
+environment variable is involved and the backend takes part in no automatic
+routing (dispatch, autotuning or trace-apply).
+
+## Operation
+
+For the token rows `t < B` of one rank with `H` heads, `h < H`, `v < 128`:
+
+```text
+S[t, h, v]        = sum_k latent[t, h, k] * w_uv[h, k, v]                 (k < 512, FP32 accumulation)
+out[t, h*128 + v] = bf16( f32(bf16(S[t, h, v])) * sigmoid_fp32(f32(gate[t, h*128 + v])) )   if valid_lengths[t // q] > 0
+out[t, h*128 + v] = +0.0                                                    if valid_lengths[t // q] <= 0
+```
+
+```python
+from flashinfer.cake_mla_value_gate import prepare_mla_value_gate
+
+runner = prepare_mla_value_gate(w_uv, max_rows=64, sigmoid_precision="fp32")  # outside capture
+runner.launch(latent, gate, valid_lengths, out)  # returns out; graph-capturable
+```
+
+| tensor | shape / dtype | layout |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `w_uv` (bound at prepare) | `[H, 512, 128]` BF16 | strides `(65536, 1, 512)`: the view of a contiguous `[H, 128, 512]` tensor (latent axis contiguous, e.g. `w_vc.contiguous().transpose(1, 2)`); 16-byte aligned |
+| `latent` | `[B, H, 512]` BF16 | contiguous, 16-byte aligned (a `[:B]` slice of a persistent buffer is fine) |
+| `gate` | `[B, H * 128]` BF16 logits | unit column stride, even row pitch `gate.stride(0) >= H * 128`, rows 4-byte aligned; e.g. `projected[:, 2112:]` of a `[B, 3648]` fused projection output |
+| `valid_lengths` | `[B // q]` int32 | contiguous |
+| `out` | `[B, H * 128]` BF16, caller-owned | contiguous, 16-byte aligned, no overlap with any input |
+
+`1 <= B <= max_rows <= 64`, `B % q == 0` (`q = rows_per_request`), all tensors on
+the device of `w_uv`.  The tests cover `H` in {1, 6, 12, 16} (12 is the
+Kimi-K3 TP8 rank) and `B` in {1..9, 16, 17, 32, 33, 48, 64}.
+
+## Numerics
+
+- The products are BF16 x BF16 (exact in FP32), accumulated in FP32 on the
+  tensor cores; the projection is rounded to BF16 (round to nearest even) once.
+- `sigmoid_precision="fp32"` is the only mode, and it is a required argument so
+  that the numerics are explicit at every call site.  The sigmoid is evaluated
+  in FP32 and multiplied unrounded with the BF16 projection; the product is
+  rounded to BF16 once.  It follows SGLang `MlaValue`'s FP32 sigmoid
+  `1 / (1 + exp(-g))`: a fast-math exponential, an approximate reciprocal
+  refined by one Newton step, and IEEE division when `1 + exp(-g)` is at least
+  `2**126` or not finite.  It is therefore within a few FP32 units in the last
+  place of the exact sigmoid, not correctly rounded.
+- The path that rounds the sigmoid to BF16 before the multiply (as a separate
+  `x * torch.sigmoid(gate)` in BF16 does) produces different bits; this API
+  does not offer it.
+- No atomics, no split-K: results are bitwise reproducible, and each row does
+  not depend on `B` (batch-invariant).
+- The tests compare against a float64 model with the same rounding boundaries
+  (BF16 projection, FP32-range sigmoid, BF16 output), with a per-element bound
+  derived from the FP32 accumulation and sigmoid error and a cap on the
+  fraction of elements that differ from the model's rounded value.
+
+## Valid and padded rows
+
+Row `t` is valid if and only if `valid_lengths[t // q] > 0`; a zero or negative
+length marks an invalid (padded) request.  An invalid row is
+written as `+0.0` (bits `0x0000`) whatever its latent or gate holds (padded
+requests may carry NaN gates).  A valid row with a NaN input gives NaN.  Rows
+`t >= B` of the caller's buffers, and gate bytes between rows (the pitch
+padding), are never read or written.  A caller whose attention shards the KV
+cache passes the global lengths: a request with an empty local shard is still
+a valid row.
+
+## Prepare, launch and CUDA graphs
+
+- `prepare_mla_value_gate` checks the device (exact SM100a / SM103a), the
+  weight's dtype, shape, strides and alignment, selects the program, loads or
+  JIT-builds it and caches the device facts.  It raises `RuntimeError` during
+  CUDA graph capture: prepare before capturing.
+- `runner.launch` checks host metadata only (shapes, strides, dtypes, devices,
+  alignment, overlap), computes the grid on the host and submits one kernel on
+  the current torch stream without allocating or synchronizing.  It may be
+  captured in a CUDA graph.
+- A replay re-reads the contents of the captured `latent`, `gate`,
+  `valid_lengths` and `w_uv` and rewrites `out`; keep their storage alive and
+  in place.  Every distinct `B` or tensor address is its own capture.
+- The runner keeps a reference to `w_uv`.  In-place updates of its contents are
+  seen by later launches.  A new or re-aliased weight tensor (for example after
+  a weight reload that replaces the storage) is not seen: call
+  `prepare_mla_value_gate` again and re-capture.
+
+## Programmatic dependent launch
+
+With `enable_pdl=True` (the default) the kernel may start while the preceding
+kernel of the stream still runs:
+
+- it reads `w_uv` **before** it waits on that kernel (`griddepcontrol.wait`),
+  so the preceding kernel must not write `w_uv`;
+- it reads `latent`, `gate` and `valid_lengths`, and writes `out`, only after
+  the wait;
+- it lets its dependents launch early (before the projection); a following
+  kernel launched with programmatic dependent launch must wait before it reads
+  `out`.
+
+With `enable_pdl=False` the launch is an ordinary stream-ordered launch.
+
+## Limitations
+
+- Exact SM100a (compute capability 10.0) and SM103a (10.3) devices only;
+  `prepare_mla_value_gate` raises `NotImplementedError` elsewhere.
+- `K = 512` latent and `N = 128` value columns per head are fixed.
+- Release wheels on PyPI omit the generated sources; the first load raises
+  there (use a nightly wheel or a source install).
+
+## Files
+
+| file | content |
+| --- | --- |
+| `cake_backend.py` | weight and launch checks, the runner, the logical argument values (hand-written) |
+| `cake_jit.py` | the host vocabulary, registry and loader glue (hand-written); the `MODULES` records are written by the exporter |
+| `build.json`, `cake_build.py` | the build manifest and the pinned loader (generated) |
+| `csrc/` | the generated kernels (`<program>_kernel.cu`), their TVM-FFI bindings (`<program>_binding.cu`) and `cake_ffi_checks.h` (generated; digest-bound by `build.json`) |
+
+Program names are `cake_mla_value_gate_<20 hex>`.  Tests:
+`pytest tests/experimental/test_cake_mla_value_gate.py`; example:
+`python examples/cake_mla_value_gate.py`; benchmark:
+`python benchmarks/bench_cake_mla_value_gate.py`.
+
+## Ownership and graduation
+
+- Owner: @yyihuang.
+- Tracking issue: flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#8795.
+- Graduation plan: the feature leaves the experimental track when (a) an
+  adapter in a real engine consumer is qualified on its target GPU, and (b) the
+  maintainers agree on the API name and on how its shape is generalized (head
+  count, decode widths, sigmoid modes).  Until then it is reviewed on the
+  experimental policy's cadence and may change or be removed.
+
+## Attribution
+
+The computation, its tiling and the valid-row and programmatic-dependent-launch
+contract are derived from SGLang's `MlaValue`
+(`python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/kimi_k3_specialized/mla_value.py` and the
+sigmoid of `python/sglang/kernels/jit/kimi_k3/primitives.py` at
+sgl-project/sglang commit `1b9493001ba7a8aa023c761dcac0db0ab3847f72`, pull

+:func:`flashinfer.cake_mla_value_gate.prepare_mla_value_gate`.
+
+Every record of ``MODULES`` is one mechanically exported program: a CUDA
+device translation unit plus a tvm-ffi binding, compiled once per
+architecture.  A record carries the host plan: the program's ``library``
+stem (its ``build.json`` entries are ``<library>_<arch>``), the architectures
+it is delivered for, the source ``module`` and ``build`` keywords it was
+rendered from, the sigmoid numerics it implements (``sigmoid``: ``"fp32"``,
+the only mode the API offers), the ``ffi_entry`` it exports and the grid rule
+:func:`launch_grid` evaluates.  The derived leaves of a record
+(``kernel_symbol``, ``launch.block``, ``launch.cluster``,
+``launch.cooperative``, ``launch.dynamic_smem_bytes``, ``launch.use_pdl``,
+``arg_plan`` and ``logical``) are rewritten by the exporter from the rendered
+binding; ``launch.use_pdl`` is ``"runtime"`` when the entry takes the
+``enable_pdl`` launch argument.  ``logical`` maps every buffer and parameter
+of ``arg_plan`` to the host vocabulary ``LOGICAL_TENSORS`` /
+``LOGICAL_SCALARS``.  Every value is a literal: FlashInfer's manifest checker
+and the exporter read this file with ``ast.literal_eval``.
+
+What to compile -- sources, digests, nvcc flags -- is recorded once in
+``build.json`` next to this file; :mod:`.cake_build` serves the library from a
+prebuilt ``aot/`` file when a builder compiled it and otherwise through
+FlashInfer's JIT from the same sources and flags.
+
+The program name ``cake_mla_value_gate_<20 hex>`` is the first twenty hex
+digits of the SHA-256 of the compact JSON ``{"build": <build keywords, sorted,
+every default spelled>, "module": <dotted source module>}`` of the kernel the
+program was rendered from; a changed keyword is a new program.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import functools
+from typing import Any
+
+# The exported architectures and the device capabilities that select them (exact match).
+ARCHES = ("sm_100a", "sm_103a")
+ARCH_BY_CAPABILITY: dict[tuple[int, int], str] = {
+    (10, 0): "sm_100a",
+    (10, 3): "sm_103a",
+}

+# contiguous ``[B, H, 512]`` tensor, ``w_uv`` the physical ``[H, 128, 512]`` view of the bound

+# ``valid_lengths`` the ``[B // q]`` int32 lengths and ``out`` the caller's contiguous ``[B, H * 128]``

+def arch_for_capability(capability: tuple[int, int]) -> str | None:
+    """The exported architecture of one device capability, if any."""
+    values = tuple(int(value) for value in capability)
+    if len(values) != 2:
+        return None
+    return ARCH_BY_CAPABILITY.get((values[0], values[1]))
+
+
+@functools.cache
+def device_arch(device_index: int) -> str | None:
+    """Exported architecture of one CUDA device, or ``None`` (the capability is immutable per process)."""
+    import torch
+
+    return arch_for_capability(tuple(torch.cuda.get_device_capability(device_index)))

+    """Names of the records delivered for ``arch`` that implement ``sigmoid``, in registry order."""
+    return [
+        name
+        for name, record in MODULES.items()
+        if arch in record["arches"] and record["sigmoid"] == sigmoid
+    ]

+    """``build.json`` library of record ``name`` built for ``arch``: ``<library>_<arch>``."""
+    record = MODULES[name]

+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"Cake MLA value gate record {name} is not delivered for {arch}; "
+            f"its architectures: {record['arches']}"
+        )

+
+
+@functools.cache
+def load(name: str, arch: str) -> Any:
+    """The loaded tvm-ffi module of record ``name`` built for ``arch``: the
+    prebuilt ``aot/`` library when a builder compiled it, else FlashInfer's JIT
+    build of the same sources and flags (``cake_build.load_library``)."""
+    from . import cake_build
+
+    return cake_build.load_library(library_name(name, arch))
+
+
+def specs_for_arch(arch: str) -> list[Any]:
+    """JIT specifications of every ``arch`` library without a prebuilt file (for
+    ahead-of-time warm-up through FlashInfer's ``build_jit_specs``)."""
+    from . import cake_build
+
+    return cake_build.jit_specs(arch)
+
+
+def launch_grid(
+    record: dict[str, Any], *, rows: int, heads: int
+) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
+    """Launch grid of one record for ``rows`` token rows of ``heads`` heads under its grid rule:
+    ``value_tiles`` -- one CTA per (``cols`` value columns, head, ``rows``-row tile):
+    ``(VALUE_DIM // cols, heads, ceil(rows / rule rows))``."""
+    rule = record["grid_rule"]
+    if rule["kind"] != "value_tiles":
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"unknown Cake MLA value gate grid rule {rule['kind']!r} in record {record['library']}"
+        )
+    cols, tile_rows = int(rule["cols"]), int(rule["rows"])
+    if cols <= 0 or VALUE_DIM % cols or tile_rows <= 0:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"record {record['library']} has an invalid value_tiles rule {rule}"
+        )
+    return (VALUE_DIM // cols, int(heads), -(-int(rows) // tile_rows))
+

+
+Tests of the experimental fused MLA value projection + sigmoid output gate
+(``flashinfer.cake_mla_value_gate.prepare_mla_value_gate``, Cake backend on
+exact SM100a / SM103a).
+
+The reference is a float64 model with the kernel's rounding boundaries: the
+projection summed exactly and rounded to BF16, the exact sigmoid, the exact
+product.  Every valid element must lie within a bound built from the FP32
+accumulation error, the FP32 sigmoid error and the final BF16 rounding, and at
+most ``MAX_MISMATCH_FRACTION`` of the valid elements may differ from the
+model's BF16-rounded value; the second check catches a wrong rounding mode or
+a BF16-rounded sigmoid that the per-element bound alone would admit.  Invalid
+rows (request length <= 0) must be +0.0 bit for bit, rows past ``B`` must stay
+untouched.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import tvm_ffi
+
+from flashinfer.cake_mla_value_gate import prepare_mla_value_gate
+from flashinfer.experimental.cake_mla_value_gate.cake_jit import ARCH_BY_CAPABILITY
+
+LATENT = 512
+VALUE = 128
+CAPACITY = 64
+# The owner's decode widths (timed) and the padding boundaries (correctness only).
+DECODE_ROWS = (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 16, 32, 48, 64)
+BOUNDARY_ROWS = (9, 17, 33)
+# Kimi-K3 TP8: 12 heads per rank; the gate is a column slice of the fused [B, 3648] projection output.
+PROD_HEADS = 12
+PROD_PITCH = 3648
+PROD_GATE_OFFSET = 2112
+
+# Accuracy contract (tolerance form).  The FP32 sigmoid's relative error against the exact sigmoid: a fixed
+# part plus a part that grows with |g| (the exponent argument -g * log2(e) is rounded to FP32 before exp2).
+SIGMOID_REL_ERROR = 2.0**-20
+SIGMOID_REL_ERROR_PER_UNIT = 2.0**-22
+# The largest fraction of valid elements whose value may differ from the model's BF16-rounded value.
+MAX_MISMATCH_FRACTION = 0.01
+# The out sentinel: rows past B must keep it.
+SENTINEL = -777.0
+# Lengths of padded requests: a request is padded iff its length is < 1.
+PADDED_LENGTHS = (0, -1, -(2**31), -4096)
+
+
+def _arch() -> str | None:
+    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
+        return None
+    return ARCH_BY_CAPABILITY.get(tuple(torch.cuda.get_device_capability()))
+
+
+requires_cuda = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="requires a CUDA device"
+)
+requires_kernel = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    _arch() is None,
+    reason="requires an exact SM100a / SM103a device (compute capability 10.0 / 10.3)",
+)
+
+
+# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Inputs
+
+
+def _generator(seed: int) -> torch.Generator:
+    return torch.Generator(device="cpu").manual_seed(seed)
+
+
+def make_w_uv(heads: int, seed: int, scale: float = 0.05) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Logical ``[H, 512, 128]`` view (strides ``(65536, 1, 512)``) of a contiguous ``[H, 128, 512]`` weight."""
+    physical = torch.randn((heads, VALUE, LATENT), generator=_generator(seed)) * scale
+    return physical.to(torch.bfloat16).cuda().transpose(1, 2)
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Case:
+    """One launch's tensors on persistent buffers of ``CAPACITY`` rows: rows past ``rows`` hold NaN
+    (inputs) or ``SENTINEL`` (output), the gate's pitch padding holds NaN."""
+
+    rows: int
+    heads: int
+    q: int
+    latent_buf: torch.Tensor
+    gate_buf: torch.Tensor
+    pitch: int
+    offset: int
+    lengths: torch.Tensor
+    out_buf: torch.Tensor
+
+    @property
+    def latent(self) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return self.latent_buf[: self.rows]
+
+    @property
+    def gate(self) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return self.gate_view(self.rows)
+
+    def gate_view(self, rows: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return self.gate_buf.as_strided(
+            (rows, self.heads * VALUE), (self.pitch, 1), self.offset
+        )
+
+    @property
+    def out(self) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return self.out_buf[: self.rows]
+
+    def args(self) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+        return self.latent, self.gate, self.lengths, self.out
+
+    def load(self, other: Case) -> None:
+        """Copy ``other``'s input contents into this case's buffers (same geometry)."""
+        self.latent_buf.copy_(other.latent_buf)
+        self.gate_buf.copy_(other.gate_buf)
+        self.lengths.copy_(other.lengths)
+
+
+def make_case(
+    rows: int,
+    heads: int,
+    *,
+    q: int = 1,
+    pitch: int | None = None,
+    offset: int = 0,
+    seed: int = 0,
+    invalid_fraction: float = 0.25,
+    gate_scale: float = 4.0,
+) -> Case:
+    width = heads * VALUE
+    pitch = width if pitch is None else pitch
+    g = _generator(1000 + seed)
+    nan = float("nan")
+    latent_buf = torch.full((CAPACITY, heads, LATENT), nan, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    latent_buf[:rows] = torch.randn((rows, heads, LATENT), generator=g).to(
+        torch.bfloat16
+    )
+    gate_buf = torch.full((offset + CAPACITY * pitch,), nan, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    gate_buf.as_strided((rows, width), (pitch, 1), offset).copy_(
+        (torch.randn((rows, width), generator=g) * gate_scale).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    )
+    requests = rows // q
+    lengths = torch.randint(1, 4096, (requests,), generator=g, dtype=torch.int32)
+    invalid = torch.rand((requests,), generator=g) < invalid_fraction
+    if requests > 1 and invalid_fraction > 0:
+        invalid[torch.randint(0, requests, (1,), generator=g)] = True
+    if invalid.all():
+        invalid[0] = False
+    # A request is padded iff its length is < 1: mix zero and negative lengths.
+    padded = torch.nonzero(invalid).flatten()
+    cycle = torch.tensor(PADDED_LENGTHS, dtype=torch.int32)
+    lengths[padded] = cycle[torch.arange(padded.numel()) % cycle.numel()]
+    # Padded requests carry garbage: NaN latent and NaN gates must still give +0.0.
+    for r in torch.nonzero(invalid).flatten().tolist():
+        latent_buf[r * q : (r + 1) * q] = nan
+        gate_buf.as_strided((rows, width), (pitch, 1), offset)[r * q : (r + 1) * q] = (
+            nan
+        )
+    out_buf = torch.full((CAPACITY, width), SENTINEL, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    return Case(
+        rows,
+        heads,
+        q,
+        latent_buf.cuda(),
+        gate_buf.cuda(),
+        pitch,
+        offset,
+        lengths.cuda(),
+        out_buf.cuda(),
+    )
+
+
+# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Reference model and checks
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Model:
+    valid: torch.Tensor  # [B] bool
+    s: torch.Tensor  # [B, H*128] exact projection (float64)
+    s_abs: torch.Tensor  # [B, H*128] sum of |products|
+    p: torch.Tensor  # [B, H*128] projection rounded to FP32, then BF16 (float64)
+    g: torch.Tensor  # [B, H*128] gate (float64)
+    sig: torch.Tensor  # [B, H*128] exact sigmoid
+    exact: torch.Tensor  # [B, H*128] p * sig
+
+
+def model(
+    latent: torch.Tensor,
+    w_uv: torch.Tensor,
+    gate: torch.Tensor,
+    lengths: torch.Tensor,
+    q: int,
+) -> Model:
+    rows, heads, _ = latent.shape
+    z, w = latent.double(), w_uv.double()
+    s = torch.einsum("bhk,hkv->bhv", z, w).reshape(rows, heads * VALUE)
+    s_abs = torch.einsum("bhk,hkv->bhv", z.abs(), w.abs()).reshape(rows, heads * VALUE)
+    p = s.float().to(torch.bfloat16).double()
+    g = gate.double()
+    sig = torch.sigmoid(g)
+    valid = lengths.long().repeat_interleave(q) > 0
+    return Model(valid, s, s_abs, p, g, sig, p * sig)
+
+
+def _rounded(x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    return x.float().to(torch.bfloat16).double()
+
+
+def check_against_model(out: torch.Tensor, m: Model, label: str = "") -> None:
+    """Invalid rows +0.0 bit for bit; valid elements within the error bound and at most
+    ``MAX_MISMATCH_FRACTION`` of the normal-range ones off the model's BF16-rounded value; NaN exactly
+    where the model has NaN."""
+    bits = out.view(torch.int16)
+    invalid = ~m.valid
+    if invalid.any():
+        assert torch.all(bits[invalid] == 0), f"{label}: an invalid row is not +0.0"
+    if not m.valid.any():
+        return
+    got = out[m.valid].double()
+    exact, p, s, s_abs, g, sig = (
+        x[m.valid] for x in (m.exact, m.p, m.s, m.s_abs, m.g, m.sig)
+    )
+    nan = torch.isnan(exact)
+    assert torch.equal(torch.isnan(got), nan), f"{label}: NaN pattern differs"
+    accumulation = LATENT * 2.0**-23 * s_abs
+    dp = accumulation + 2.0**-7 * (s.abs() + accumulation)
+    sig_rel = SIGMOID_REL_ERROR + SIGMOID_REL_ERROR_PER_UNIT * g.abs().clamp(max=128.0)
+    bound = sig * dp + (p.abs() + dp) * sig * sig_rel
+    tol = bound + 2.0**-8 * (exact.abs() + bound) + (p.abs() + 1.0) * 2.0**-126
+    err = (got - exact).abs()
+    bad = ~nan & ~(err <= tol)
+    if bad.any():
+        idx = torch.nonzero(bad)[0].tolist()
+        raise AssertionError(
+            f"{label}: {int(bad.sum())} elements outside the bound; first at {idx}: "
+            f"got {got[tuple(idx)].item()!r}, model {exact[tuple(idx)].item()!r}, "
+            f"tol {tol[tuple(idx)].item()!r}, p {p[tuple(idx)].item()!r}, g {g[tuple(idx)].item()!r}"
+        )
+    # Subnormal sigmoids and products depend on the kernel's flush-to-zero choices; the absolute
+    # floor of the bound covers them, the rounding statistics count the normal range only.
+    counted = ~nan & (sig >= 2.0**-126) & (exact.abs() >= 2.0**-126)
+    mismatch = (got != _rounded(exact)) & counted
+    fraction = float(mismatch.sum()) / max(1, int(counted.sum()))
+    assert fraction <= MAX_MISMATCH_FRACTION, (
+        f"{label}: {fraction:.4%} of the valid elements differ from the model's BF16 value"
+    )
+
+
+def check_case(
+    case: Case, w_uv: torch.Tensor, label: str, inputs: Case | None = None
+) -> None:
+    """``case.out`` against the model of ``inputs`` (default: ``case``'s own inputs); rows past ``B`` of
+    ``case.out_buf`` must keep the sentinel."""
+    src = case if inputs is None else inputs
+    check_against_model(
+        case.out, model(src.latent, w_uv, src.gate, src.lengths, src.q), label
+    )
+    tail = case.out_buf[case.rows :]
+    assert torch.all(tail == SENTINEL), f"{label}: rows past B were written"
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
+def prod_w_uv() -> torch.Tensor:
+    return make_w_uv(PROD_HEADS, seed=7)
+
+
+def _prepare(w_uv: torch.Tensor, **kwargs):
+    kwargs.setdefault("max_rows", CAPACITY)
+    kwargs.setdefault("sigmoid_precision", "fp32")
+    return prepare_mla_value_gate(w_uv, **kwargs)
+
+
+# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Accuracy over the shape list
+
+
+@requires_kernel
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("rows", DECODE_ROWS + BOUNDARY_ROWS)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "pitch, offset",
+    [(PROD_PITCH, PROD_GATE_OFFSET), (PROD_HEADS * VALUE, 0)],
+    ids=["pitch3648_off2112", "pitch1536"],
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("enable_pdl", [True, False])
+def test_accuracy_production_heads(prod_w_uv, rows, pitch, offset, enable_pdl):
+    runner = _prepare(prod_w_uv, enable_pdl=enable_pdl)
+    case = make_case(rows, PROD_HEADS, pitch=pitch, offset=offset, seed=rows)

+# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Programmatic dependent launch: a predecessor that lets its dependents start before it writes,
+# and a successor that starts early and waits before it reads.
+
+_SPIN_CYCLES = 1_000_000  # about half a millisecond
+
+_PROBE_SOURCE = r"""
+#include <cuda_runtime.h>
+#include <tvm/ffi/container/tensor.h>
+#include <tvm/ffi/error.h>
+#include <tvm/ffi/extra/c_env_api.h>
+#include <tvm/ffi/function.h>
+
+#include <cstdint>
+
+using tvm::ffi::TensorView;
+
+struct Copies {
+  uint8_t* dst[4];
+  const uint8_t* src[4];
+  int64_t bytes[4];
+};
+
+__global__ void TriggerSpinCopyKernel(Copies copies, int64_t spin_cycles) {
+  // Let the dependent launch start now, before anything is written.
+  asm volatile("griddepcontrol.launch_dependents;" ::: "memory");
+  const int64_t start = clock64();
+  while (clock64() - start < spin_cycles) {
+  }
+  const int64_t stride = int64_t(gridDim.x) * blockDim.x;
+  for (int c = 0; c < 4; ++c) {
+    for (int64_t i = blockIdx.x * int64_t(blockDim.x) + threadIdx.x; i < copies.bytes[c]; i += stride) {
+      copies.dst[c][i] = copies.src[c][i];
+    }
+  }
+}
+
+__global__ void WaitCopyKernel(uint8_t* dst, const uint8_t* src, int64_t bytes) {
+  asm volatile("griddepcontrol.wait;" ::: "memory");
+  const int64_t stride = int64_t(gridDim.x) * blockDim.x;
+  for (int64_t i = blockIdx.x * int64_t(blockDim.x) + threadIdx.x; i < bytes; i += stride) {
+    dst[i] = src[i];
+  }
+}
+
+static int64_t Bytes(const TensorView& t) { return t.numel() * ((t.dtype().bits + 7) / 8); }
+
+static cudaStream_t StreamOf(const TensorView& t) {
+  return static_cast<cudaStream_t>(TVMFFIEnvGetStream(t.device().device_type, t.device().device_id));
+}
+
+// Copies src_i over dst_i (whole contiguous tensors) after triggering its dependents and spinning.
+void DelayedCopies(TensorView d0, TensorView s0, TensorView d1, TensorView s1, TensorView d2, TensorView s2,
+                   TensorView d3, TensorView s3, int64_t spin_cycles) {
+  Copies copies{};
+  const TensorView* pairs[4][2] = {{&d0, &s0}, {&d1, &s1}, {&d2, &s2}, {&d3, &s3}};
+  for (int c = 0; c < 4; ++c) {
+    const TensorView& d = *pairs[c][0];
+    const TensorView& s = *pairs[c][1];
+    TVM_FFI_ICHECK(d.IsContiguous() && s.IsContiguous() && Bytes(d) == Bytes(s)) << "pair " << c;
+    copies.dst[c] = static_cast<uint8_t*>(d.data_ptr()) + d.byte_offset();
+    copies.src[c] = static_cast<const uint8_t*>(s.data_ptr()) + s.byte_offset();
+    copies.bytes[c] = Bytes(d);
+  }
+  int sms = 0;
+  TVM_FFI_ICHECK(cudaDeviceGetAttribute(&sms, cudaDevAttrMultiProcessorCount, d0.device().device_id) ==
+                 cudaSuccess);
+  // One resident CTA per SM: every CTA triggers before a dependent can take a slot.
+  TriggerSpinCopyKernel<<<sms, 256, 0, StreamOf(d0)>>>(copies, spin_cycles);
+  const cudaError_t status = cudaGetLastError();
+  TVM_FFI_ICHECK(status == cudaSuccess) << cudaGetErrorString(status);
+}
+
+// Copies src over dst, launched with programmatic dependent launch; waits on its predecessor first.
+void WaitThenCopy(TensorView dst, TensorView src) {
+  TVM_FFI_ICHECK(dst.IsContiguous() && src.IsContiguous() && Bytes(dst) == Bytes(src));
+  uint8_t* d = static_cast<uint8_t*>(dst.data_ptr()) + dst.byte_offset();
+  const uint8_t* s = static_cast<const uint8_t*>(src.data_ptr()) + src.byte_offset();
+  int64_t bytes = Bytes(dst);
+  cudaLaunchConfig_t config{};
+  config.gridDim = dim3(32, 1, 1);
+  config.blockDim = dim3(256, 1, 1);
+  config.dynamicSmemBytes = 0;
+  config.stream = StreamOf(dst);
+  cudaLaunchAttribute attrs[1] = {};
+  attrs[0].id = cudaLaunchAttributeProgrammaticStreamSerialization;
+  attrs[0].val.programmaticStreamSerializationAllowed = 1;
+  config.attrs = attrs;
+  config.numAttrs = 1;
+  const cudaError_t status = cudaLaunchKernelEx(&config, WaitCopyKernel, d, s, bytes);
+  TVM_FFI_ICHECK(status == cudaSuccess) << cudaGetErrorString(status);
+}
+
+TVM_FFI_DLL_EXPORT_TYPED_FUNC(delayed_copies, DelayedCopies);
+TVM_FFI_DLL_EXPORT_TYPED_FUNC(wait_then_copy, WaitThenCopy);
+"""
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
+def probe():
+    from flashinfer.jit import env as jit_env
+    from flashinfer.jit.core import gen_jit_spec, sm100a_nvcc_flags, sm103a_nvcc_flags
+    from flashinfer.jit.utils import write_if_different
+
+    arch = _arch()
+    if arch is None:
+        pytest.skip("requires an exact SM100a / SM103a device")
+    flags = {"sm_100a": sm100a_nvcc_flags, "sm_103a": sm103a_nvcc_flags}[arch]
+    name = f"test_cake_mla_value_gate_pdl_probe_{arch}"
+    source = jit_env.FLASHINFER_GEN_SRC_DIR / name / "probe.cu"
+    write_if_different(source, _PROBE_SOURCE)
+    return gen_jit_spec(name, [source], extra_cuda_cflags=flags).build_and_load()
+
+
+class _PdlChain:
+    """predecessor (triggers, spins, then writes the inputs and snapshots ``out``) -> the PDL runner ->
+    successor (PDL launch, waits, then copies ``out``), on the current stream."""
+
+    def __init__(self, probe, runner, case: Case) -> None:
+        self.probe, self.runner, self.case = probe, runner, case
+        self.staged = make_case(
+            case.rows, case.heads, pitch=case.pitch, offset=case.offset, seed=0
+        )
+        self.previous_out = torch.empty_like(case.out_buf)
+        self.snapshot = torch.empty_like(case.out_buf)
+        self.copied = torch.empty_like(case.out_buf)
+
+    def stage(self, seed: int) -> Case:
+        staged = make_case(
+            self.case.rows,
+            self.case.heads,
+            pitch=self.case.pitch,
+            offset=self.case.offset,
+            seed=seed,
+        )
+        self.staged.load(staged)
+        # The buffers the chain overwrites hold stale contents: the previous inputs and a known old output.
+        self.previous_out.copy_(
+            torch.randn(self.previous_out.shape, generator=_generator(seed)).to(
+                torch.bfloat16
+            )
+        )
+        self.case.out_buf.copy_(self.previous_out)
+        return staged
+
+    def run(self) -> None:
+        c, s = self.case, self.staged
+        with tvm_ffi.use_torch_stream():
+            self.probe.delayed_copies(
+                c.latent_buf, s.latent_buf, c.gate_buf, s.gate_buf, c.lengths, s.lengths,
+                self.snapshot, c.out_buf, _SPIN_CYCLES,
+            )  # fmt: skip
+        self.runner.launch(*c.args())
+        with tvm_ffi.use_torch_stream():
+            self.probe.wait_then_copy(self.copied, c.out_buf)
+
+    def check(self, staged: Case, w_uv: torch.Tensor, label: str) -> None:
+        c = self.case
+        # The runner waited for the predecessor's writes before reading its inputs ...
+        check_against_model(
+            c.out, model(staged.latent, w_uv, staged.gate, staged.lengths, c.q), label
+        )
+        plain = torch.full_like(c.out_buf, SENTINEL)
+        _prepare(w_uv, enable_pdl=False).launch(
+            staged.latent, staged.gate, staged.lengths, plain[: c.rows]
+        )
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        assert torch.equal(
+            c.out.view(torch.int16), plain[: c.rows].view(torch.int16)
+        ), label
+        # ... did not write out before the predecessor read it ...
+        assert torch.equal(
+            self.snapshot.view(torch.int16), self.previous_out.view(torch.int16)
+        ), label
+        # ... and the successor saw the finished output.
+        assert torch.equal(
+            self.copied.view(torch.int16), c.out_buf.view(torch.int16)
+        ), label
+
+
+@requires_kernel
+def test_pdl_predecessor_and_successor_eager(probe, prod_w_uv):
+    case = make_case(64, PROD_HEADS, pitch=PROD_PITCH, offset=PROD_GATE_OFFSET, seed=60)
+    chain = _PdlChain(probe, _prepare(prod_w_uv, enable_pdl=True), case)
+    for seed in (61, 62, 63):
+        staged = chain.stage(seed)
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        chain.run()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        chain.check(staged, prod_w_uv, f"eager {seed}")
+
+
+@requires_kernel
+def test_pdl_predecessor_and_successor_graph(probe, prod_w_uv):
+    case = make_case(32, PROD_HEADS, pitch=PROD_PITCH, offset=PROD_GATE_OFFSET, seed=70)
+    chain = _PdlChain(probe, _prepare(prod_w_uv, enable_pdl=True), case)
+    chain.stage(71)
+    side = torch.cuda.Stream()
+    side.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+    with torch.cuda.stream(side):
+        chain.run()  # warm-up outside capture
+    torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(side)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+        chain.run()
+    for seed in (72, 73, 74):
+        staged = chain.stage(seed)
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        graph.replay()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        chain.check(staged, prod_w_uv, f"graph {seed}")
